_comment: Canonical 2D transform / coordinate-system vocabulary. This is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for how a node's world transform is built from parent + local parts. The rest of the project (motion_runtime.scene, scene.scene_graph, renderers) MUST interpret a transform through this vocabulary so that 'the Agent describes a local coordinate system, the Runtime composes it the same way everywhere' holds. Before this contract, the two scene systems disagreed: motion_runtime used a full affine (rotation honoured), scene.scene_graph used scalar inheritance (rotation ignored), so a rotated node had two different world boxes.

model.representation: 2D affine, 6-tuple (a,b,c,d,e,f) = | a c e ; b d f ; 0 0 1 |
model.point_apply: (x', y') = (a*x + c*y + e, b*x + d*y + f)
model.parent_child: world = parent_world @ local  (local applied first, then parent)
model.rotation_units: degrees, clockwise-positive in a y-down pixel space
model.scale: uniform by default; anisotropic scale_y is allowed but off the default path

bounding_box._comment: A node's world box is the axis-aligned bounds of its four transformed corners, so rotation is reflected in the box.

conventions.parent_move: moving a parent MUST move every descendant's world transform (no per-child absolute re-edit)
conventions.rotation_inheritance: child world rotation = sum of the chain's rotations (via matrix composition)
conventions.opacity_inheritance: child world opacity = product of the chain's opacities
conventions.visibility_inheritance: a node is visible only if every node in its chain is visible

known_divergences._comment: Tracked, not silently 'fixed'. Quantified by runtime/geometry/audit.py.
known_divergences.scene.scene_graph.world_box: scalar inheritance: world_box = [ox, oy, w*s, h*s] and world_origin offsets by parent scale only -> rotation ignored (matches canonical only when every chain rotation is 0)
